description.narrative: The project is implemented in Palestine. The main outcome areas it contributes to are Countering the threats to democracy and human rights, Promoting peace and dialogue mitigating armed conflict and social tensions, and Opposing the backlash increasing gender equality. The main rights holders are youth, often in higher education, that have the potential to be young leaders. Through trainings, advanced leadership courses, youth conferences and dialogue meetings with political leaders, the project aims to achieve progressive development within the outcome areas.Project OrganisationsThe project is a cooperation between Palestinian Peace Coalition (Geneva Initiative) and the Palme Center. The project is implemented with the support of Anna Lindh Memorial Fund. The Palestinian Peace Coalition is the Palestinian wing of the Israeli-palestinian civil society network Geneva Initative that collaborates for dialogue and a two-state solution of the Israeli-palestinian conflict. They work to support moderate voices for dialogue and peace in the face of increasing poliarisation. The Anna Lindh Memorial Fund is not a Palme Center member organisation but is close to the Labour Movement. They work to encourage and support those who work for a more humane and just world in the spirit of the late Anna Lindh.Other Donors to the OrganisationPPC are or have recently been supported financially by Swiss FDFA, the EU Peacebuilding Initiative, Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Finish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Irish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and SHARE Foundation. Coordination with other donors will be explored, and especially discussions with PPCs Israeli counterpart.Project ObjectivePPC aims to educate and enhance skills of emerging young leaders so that they can have more influence on decision makers and on their community. This includes awareness raising and capacity building that also includes non-violence, women empowerment and upholding the principles of democracy.Actor groupsDecision Makers: policy makers, mid-level and junior advisors, and opinion shapers (including journalists), loca community leaders and political parties, extreme religious actors. Actors working in cooperation: civil society activists and CSO networks. This includes the two-state solution coalition consisting of 22 civil society organisations, as well as local organisations on the West Bank and Gaza strip and in Jerusalem. Rights Holders: young and promising leaders. The target group includes religious and political minotirites, young leaders from refugee camps and women.
